title: Free Energy of Non-uniform Disordered Superconductors
abstract: We extend the Luttinger-Ward free energy functional to disordered superconductors and superfluids with arbitrary scattering mechanisms, including both impurity disorder and the presence of interfaces. The disorder is taken into account within the self-consistent $t$-matrix approximation, thus allowing for arbitrary impurity scattering strengths. It is shown that both the interface and the impurity scattering self-energy appear in the functional only implicitly, through self-consistently determined fermionic propagators. The free energy functional is formulated in terms of a generalized integral in the complex energy plane, which encompasses formulations both in terms of retarded/advanced propagators and in terms of Matsubara Green's functions by appropriately choosing the integration path. It can be applied, e.g., to spatially non-uniform and hybrid systems, triplet and other unconventional condensates, and strongly-correlated Fermi liquids. A particularly useful formulation in terms of the quasiclassical propagators is applied to unconventional non-uniform singlet and triplet superconductors and superfluids in an external Zeeman magnetic field.
summary: This work develops a generalized free energy functional for disordered and non-uniform superconductors by extending the Luttinger-Ward formalism. It incorporates disorder effects via the self-consistent t-matrix approximation and handles spatial variations using complex contour integration. The resulting theory provides a powerful tool to calculate superconducting properties in complex materials, such as those with interfaces or magnetic fields.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive the free energy functional for superconducting systems, specifically accounting for the effects of disorder and spatial non-uniformities.
main_result: The free energy functional is formulated generally using a complex energy plane integral, applicable to various unconventional superconductors and hybrid systems.
method: The derivation extends the Luttinger-Ward functional, employing the self-consistent t-matrix approximation for disorder and utilizing contour integration in the complex energy plane to unify different formalisms.
model_or_system: The system under study is disordered superconductors and superfluids, including unconventional singlet and triplet condensates, potentially subjected to external Zeeman magnetic fields or interfaces.
key_observables: Free energy ($\Omega$), induced charge density ($ho_{	ext{ind}}$), orbital current ($\mathbf{J}_{	ext{orb}}$), and magnetization ($\mathbf{M}_{	ext{spin}}$).
important_parameters: Impurity scattering strengths, interface scattering types (specular vs. diffuse), external magnetic fields ($\mathbf{H}$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The theory assumes weak-coupling superconductivity and relies on self-consistent approximations for disorder and the inclusion of electromagnetic potentials perturbatively.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spatial profiles of mean-field order parameters and magnetization near interfaces, comparing results for specular versus diffuse scattering.
paper_structure: The structure involves extending the Luttinger-Ward functional, deriving self-consistency equations for the self-energy using the t-matrix approximation, converting Matsubara sums to complex contour integrals, and finally applying the formalism to calculate electromagnetic contributions and pair-breaking energies.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework for calculating thermodynamic potentials in the presence of disorder and spatial gradients is highly relevant for understanding complex many-body systems, bridging concepts from BCS theory to modern condensed matter theory.
